title: Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans: Conditions on Which Coverage Is Written
content:
**1. Value of the piece.** Coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans is written only on a piece whose pre-tax selling price falls between the smallest and the largest item value that coverage admits.

**2. Purchase window.** A protection plan is quoted only when the covered piece was sold within the purchase window in calendar days the coverage allows, counted from the date the covered piece was sold. The purchase window is counted in whole calendar days from the day of sale, that day counting as day zero, weekends and store holidays included, and no substitution of business days is made. A plan quoted on the last day of the window is quoted within it.

**3. Appraisal above a stated value.** Above the item value the coverage sets, a current appraisal must already be on file for the piece before the plan is written, and the customer's own belief about what the piece is worth never stands in for it.

**4. Premium.** The premium is the coverage's share of the item value and may be added to a promotional financing plan only on the coverage that admits it.

**5. When coverage begins.** Coverage begins once the waiting period has run from the day the plan was bought, and nothing that happened before coverage began is answered for.

## Evidence for clauses 2 and 3

What is verified is the record, not the account given at the counter. For the purchase window the till transaction the piece was sold on and the covered item reference tie the quote to the sale, and the date the piece was sold is read from the plan record. For the appraisal condition the covered item reference ties the report on file to the piece being covered. Both are tested before the plan is written.

## Boundary readings of the purchase window

Take a coverage whose purchase window is 30 calendar days (a hypothetical input). A piece sold on the first of a month and quoted on the thirty-first day counting the day of sale as day zero falls on the last day of the window, and the plan is quoted. The same piece quoted one day later falls outside the window, and no plan is quoted on it. Neither reading changes where the intervening days fall in the week.

## Premium on hypothetical inputs

A piece sold pre-tax at 2000.00 USD under coverage whose plan price is 11.0 percent of the item value (both hypothetical inputs) carries a premium of 220.00 USD, the item value taken at that percentage and the result taken to two decimal places.
